exercises.title: Tracing 1 — which motivation for tracing?
exercises.problemHtml:
Wiegers’ motivations for tracing: finding missing requirements · finding unnecessary requirements · certification and compliance · change impact analysis · maintenance · project tracking · reengineering · reuse · testing. Name the motivation behind each use of the trace data.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Các lý do để truy vết. Gọi tên lý do đằng sau từng cách dùng dữ liệu truy vết.

Yêu cầu

  • Trả lời mọi câu trong khung trả lời rồi bấm Nộp.
  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.

o.s: A business requirement traces to no user requirement.
A functional requirement traces to no user or business requirement.
The auditor asks to see that every safety requirement is implemented and tested.
A tax rule changes; the team finds every design element and code module that handles it.
Links from requirements to code are missing for 12 requirements — that work is not done yet.
The functions of the 1998 system are listed and traced into the new system’s requirements.
A test fails; the team identifies which requirement is not satisfied.
The team takes the payment requirements, design and code of one product into another.

bang.giaiThich: The same links serve many purposes — which is why tracing pays off when done consistently.

exercises.title: Tracing 2 — how much tracing?
exercises.problemHtml:
Figure 29-2 shows many possible trace relationships — you do not need them all. Do a cost-benefit analysis: often most of the benefit comes from a few links (e.g. system tests back to functional or user requirements). Each requirement must have a unique, persistent label for tracing to work.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:

exercises.title: Tracing 3 — who supplies the trace links?
exercises.problemHtml:
Trace links should be defined by whoever has the knowledge (Table 29-3): the BA knows links between needs and requirements; developers know links between requirements and design/code; testers know links between requirements and tests.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Tracing 4 — tracing nonfunctional requirements
exercises.problemHtml:
Nonfunctional requirements often do not trace to one piece of code: a response-time requirement may dictate hardware, algorithms, database structure or architecture; a portability requirement may restrict language features. Some quality attributes do produce code (e.g. security functions such as login lock-out) — trace those to it.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

# Tracing 4 — tracing nonfunctional requirements — answer key

1. "95% of searches in under 2 seconds" most likely traces to…"95% lượt tìm dưới 2 giây" nhiều khả năng truy tới…
   Answer: d) architecture and design decisions (indexes, caching, hardware) and performance tests
   Quality → architecture + tests.VI: Chất lượng → kiến trúc + test.

   Answer: d) specific code (the lock-out function) and its tests
   This quality requirement produces code.VI: Yêu cầu chất lượng này sinh ra code.
